solution.summary: The bid delivers a hosted, cloud-based accounting and financial reporting platform for the City of Colfax, configured to replace the City's current Tyler Technologies Fund Balance modules (Accounts Payable with 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions and approvals, Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing and Business Licensing) for five users, plus a full implementation services wrap. Delivery runs in four phases mirroring the RFP's task structure: an approach and project-management phase (dedicated project manager, weekly progress/budget/timeline meetings, audit-aware account structure recommendation), a build-and-migrate phase (configuration, financial report writing, import of five years of history, coordination with Accounting and IT), a training phase (power-user and all-staff training with manuals and at least one recorded session), and a twelve-month post-go-live support phase (help desk, automated update notices, annual 1099/W-2 e-filing support). The work is a build-and-configure engagement on a vendor-hosted subscription, not a custom software development, and is sequenced to reach the City's July 1, 2026 go-live at the start of its fiscal year. The team is a named implementation project manager, functional consultants per module, a report-writing specialist, a data migration engineer, a trainer, and an account manager who carries the relationship through renewal. A governance and compliance workstream runs alongside delivery to carry the RFP's contractual, insurance, certification, pricing-breakout and disclosure obligations, and the proposal itself is assembled to the RFP's required tab order and page limits.

components.title: Project management, governance and compliance obligations
components.description: A dedicated project manager runs the engagement with a written personnel management plan naming the PM, technical staff and their roles, and holds weekly meetings that track progress, budget and timeline against a published schedule. The same workstream owns the RFP's contractual and administrative obligations: no additional or modified terms are submitted with the proposal and no attempt is made to alter or delete the bar on modified terms; the team observes the no-contact rule during evaluation and accepts that a violation disqualifies it; it accepts that all RFP terms are enforceable contract conditions and that 'shall', 'must' and 'requirements' are binding; it notifies the City within 30 days of any condition materially altering the financial certification and notifies the Contract Lead within 15 days of material changes to the financial-condition representations; and it gives written notice if personnel relocate outside the United States. The bid team also files written questions by July 31, 2025, holds September 25, 2025 for virtual finalist interviews, and absorbs all proposal and interview costs without reimbursement.

claims.text: The City's fiscal year ends June 30, which is why the go-live target is July 1, 2026.
The City has 11 full-time employees with one position vacant plus one part-time/seasonal/contract employee, so the vendor must carry most implementation workload.

components.title: Hosted accounting and financial reporting platform
components.description: A cloud-hosted subscription platform configured to cover every module the City uses today: Accounts Payable including 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions and purchase orders with approval routing; Accounts Receivable; General Ledger; Payroll; Utility Billing; and Business Licensing. Transactions post systematically through the general ledger with budgeting and forecasting tools, and the reporting layer produces standard and ad hoc reports and analysis for Council and management decision-making. The system retains transaction detail, approval trails and documentation so records remain auditable for future reference, and it is licensed for the City's five users with a documented path to add licenses as staffing changes. The proposal identifies license types by level of use and states where any additional application or third-party vendor is used to meet a requirement.

claims.text: The City currently runs Tyler Technologies Fund Balance with Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, General Ledger, Payroll, Utility Billing and Business Licensing modules and five users.

components.title: Account structure design and financial report writing
components.description: Consultants with public-sector audit and reporting expertise review the City's current chart of accounts and recommend an account structure that supports auditable reporting, fund accounting and the City's budget-to-actual and financial statement needs. The team then writes the City's financial reports in the new system, including the standard reports the City produces today and the analysis views its decision-makers rely on, and documents the numbering scheme and customization options so the City can maintain the structure itself. Account number customization is described concretely in the proposal: segment definitions, format and length, and how the City can define and change its own numbering.

components.title: Data migration of five years of history
components.description: The team extracts, maps, cleans and loads the prior five years of financial history from the City's current system into the new platform, with reconciliation and control totals signed off by Accounting before cutover. Migration runs in a rehearsal pass followed by a final load, and the team works directly with Accounting and IT on file formats, timing and validation so the transition causes minimal downtime and operational impact. The proposal states the assumed source system, record volumes and file formats used to size the effort.

claims.text: The prior five years of data must be imported for history.

components.title: Implementation plan, schedule and go-live
components.description: A phased implementation plan and task sequence sized to reach go-live on July 1, 2026, aligned to the start of the City's fiscal year, with milestones for configuration, migration, parallel testing, training and cutover. The plan names key implementation personnel, describes support levels during implementation and for recurring licenses and services, and sets out the client engagement approach including the role of an account manager. Contingency is built into the schedule so a late contract award compresses scope rather than the go-live date.

claims.text: The City's stated go-live target is July 1, 2026, with the project starting soon after contract award and negotiation.

components.title: Training and change management
components.description: Personalized power-user training and manuals for the City's finance staff, plus at least one recorded training session and a written manual made available to all staff, delivered in person, virtually or as standard recordings by license level as the City prefers. Training is scheduled before go-live on configured data and repeated after cutover, and the recorded sessions and manuals stay with the City as reference material. The approach accounts for a small staff carrying full-time duties during the transition.

claims.text: The City's small staff and single vacancy mean training must fit around full-time operational duties.

components.title: Ongoing support, help desk and annual e-filing
components.description: Twelve months of post-implementation support included in the base price, covering a help desk with a ticketing system that prioritizes and tracks requests, named support hours, and escalation paths. The vendor pushes automated software updates and issues change notices so the City knows what changed and when, and provides annual 1099 and W-2 e-filing support each filing season. Support continues through annual contract renewals with the same account manager, and the proposal states response-time commitments so the City can score the technical support criterion.

components.title: Security, data protection and financial-condition assurance
components.description: A security documentation package for Attachment G describing the controls protecting the City's financial data: encryption in transit and at rest, role-based access, multi-factor authentication, segregation of duties, logging and monitoring, backup and recovery, and incident response, mapped to a recognized framework so the City can compare it to its expectations. The bid also supplies Attachment D certification of financial stability with an unqualified audit opinion and no liens or disqualifying litigation, signed by an authorized representative, and Attachment E proof of workers compensation and commercial general liability coverage.

components.title: Price proposal and cost transparency
components.description: Attachment A is completed as the price proposal cover sheet and references the specific tasks and deliverables in the RFP's scope of work. The price breaks out the implementation fee, recurring fees, license fees, and support costs during implementation separately from post-implementation, plus an estimate for any additional applications or vendors. The total price covers all materials, supplies and travel, reimbursable expenses are capped at a stated figure rather than left unlimited, and the total price proposal amount is stated as a single figure. The price is submitted as final and is not altered during clarification.

components.title: Proposal assembly, references and demonstrations
components.description: The bid team assembles the response in the RFP's required tab order within the page allowance, with a signed original hard copy and a digital copy emailed to accounting@colfax-ca.gov under the required subject line before the August 28, 2025 4:00 PM PST deadline. The package includes a completed Attachment F software abilities spreadsheet, license types by level of use, the account-number customization description, disclosure of any additional applications or vendors, and the availability of virtual product demonstrations. It carries at least three references for similar work with valid e-mail addresses and full contact detail, a local referral able to host an in-person demonstration, and firm qualifications and key personnel summaries.

claims.text: Proposals are due August 28, 2025 at 4:00 PM PST, with finalist interviews on September 25, 2025 and award targeted for October 22, 2025.

assumptions.text: All six modules the City runs today, including 1099 filing, purchasing requisitions and purchase orders with approvals, are assumed to be required functionality of the new system and are replaced one-for-one.
Five users is assumed to be the licensed quantity at go-live, with additional named-user licenses priced as an option rather than included in the base.
July 1, 2026 is treated as a firm go-live commitment, with implementation assumed to begin within 30 days of the October 22, 2025 award target.
The twelve months of post-implementation support is assumed to start at go-live and to be included in the base price rather than priced as an option.

The five-year data migration is assumed to draw from the City's current Tyler Technologies Fund Balance system in its standard export formats, with the City supplying extracts and the vendor performing mapping and cleaning.
The reimbursable expense cap is assumed to be a respondent-proposed figure stated in Attachment A, set at a level covering travel for on-site training and cutover support.
The total price proposal amount is assumed to be the sum of the total price for all services and deliverables plus the capped reimbursable expenses, stated as one figure.
The Attachment F software abilities spreadsheet is assumed to match the functional scope described in the RFP's scope of work, and is completed against that scope pending the City's separate file.

The City's standard contract is assumed to be its General Contract Terms and Conditions without material deviation, so no exceptions are raised in the proposal and any concerns are raised as written questions by July 31, 2025.
Where the 30-day and 15-day financial-certification notice periods conflict, the shorter 15-day period to the Contract Lead is assumed to govern, with the City also notified within 30 days.
Insurance is assumed to be carried at limits customary for a municipal software and services contract, with certificates naming the City as additional insured, pending the City's stated limits.
Attachment G documentation is assumed to be accepted as a written control narrative mapped to a recognized security framework, since the RFP names no standard.
The account manager role is assumed to be a named, dedicated contact included in the base price rather than an optional or on-site resource.
The 20-page limit is treated as binding, with the cover letter and appendices kept within their separate allowances.
The hard copy is assumed to be delivered to the 33 S. Main Street address to be physically received by the 4:00 PM PST deadline, with the emailed copy sent before the same time.
